what_its_for: Paromomycin is an antibiotic used to treat certain intestinal infections caused by parasites, such as intestinal amebiasis (an infection caused by a parasite called Entamoeba histolytica) and tapeworm infections. It works by killing or stopping the growth of parasites in your intestines.
how_to_take: Take paromomycin capsules by mouth with meals to help reduce stomach upset. Swallow the capsules whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew the capsules unless your doctor tells you to. Take this medicine exactly as your doctor prescribed, and finish the entire course of treatment even if you start to feel better. Stopping early may allow the infection to come back.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your weight, the type of infection, and your overall health. The usual adult dose for intestinal amebiasis is 25 to 35 mg per kilogram of body weight per day, divided into three doses taken with meals for 5 to 10 days. For tapeworm infections, dosing is different and your doctor will give you specific instructions. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store paromomycin capsules at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the capsules away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the label. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely by following your local pharmacy take-back program guidelines.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking paromomycin if you have a known bowel blockage or serious kidney disease, unless your doctor specifically tells you it is safe. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you are taking, as paromomycin may interact with some antibiotics and other drugs. Avoid skipping doses or stopping treatment early, as this can make the infection harder to treat. Do not share your medicine with others, even if they have similar symptoms.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: severe or bloody diarrhea, severe stomach pain or cramping, hearing loss or ringing in your ears, dizziness or loss of balance, signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination or swelling in your legs or ankles, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also contact your doctor if your symptoms do not improve after finishing your treatment or if they get worse.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting paromomycin, but it is very important to take the full course of treatment as prescribed. Intestinal parasite infections may take the full 5 to 10 days of treatment to be completely cleared. Your doctor may want to do follow-up stool tests after treatment to make sure the infection is fully gone.
special_populations: Kidney disease: Use with caution if you have kidney problems, as paromomycin can build up in the body and cause serious side effects including hearing loss. Your doctor may need to monitor your kidney function closely. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as the safety of paromomycin during pregnancy has not been fully established. However, it is sometimes used during pregnancy for certain infections under close medical supervision. Breastfeeding: It is not known if paromomycin passes into breast milk in significant amounts. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medicine. Children: Paromomycin can be used in children, but the dose will be carefully calculated based on your child's weight. Always follow your pediatrician's instructions. Elderly: Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of paromomycin, especially effects on the kidneys and hearing. Your doctor may monitor you more closely.
